## 🎯 Objectives

- Understand how to use the Quarto journal and thesis templates.
- Manage references and citations.
- Add and customize code chunks, equations, figures, and tables in Quarto.

## Quarto Template for Journal Paper

With Quarto, you can make journal papers.

You can use this as a template to create an article. or

You may also use this format with an existing Quarto project or document.

Here, we are going to use the template for **Journal of Statistical Software**

## Let's begin..

### Creating a New Article

```quarto use template quarto-journals/jss```

This will install the extension and create an example qmd file and bibiography that you can use as a starting place for your article.

### Installation For Existing Document

You may also use this format with an existing Quarto project or document. From the quarto project or document directory, run the following command to install this format:

```quarto add quarto-journals/jss```

---

#### How to render...

To use the format, you can use the format names `jss-pdf` and `jss-html`. For example:

```quarto render article.qmd --to jss-pdf```

or in your document yaml

```yaml
format:
  pdf: default
  jss-pdf:
    keep-tex: true    
```

### Resource to find journal templates

https://github.com/quarto-journals

This is a Quarto template that assists you in creating a Monash University thesis.

This will install the extension and create the files that you can use as a starting place for your thesis.

## 📚 Adding a Bibliography to `.qmd` Files

````markdown
### 1. Create a `.bib` File (BibTeX Format)

```bibtex
@article{smith2021,
  title = {A Method for Data Analysis},
  author = {Smith, Jane},
  journal = {Journal of Statistics},
  year = {2021}
}
````

💡 Save as: `references.bib`

---

### 2. Link the `.bib` File in YAML

```yaml
bibliography: references.bib
csl: apa.csl  # Optional: adds citation style (e.g., APA, IEEE)
```

### 3. Cite in the Text

```markdown
As shown in recent work [@smith2021], the method is effective.
```

🔄 Quarto will automatically format the in-text citation and generate a reference list.

### 🔍 Tips

* Download CSL files from [zotero.org/styles](https://www.zotero.org/styles)
* You can also use reference managers (Zotero, Mendeley) to export `.bib` files.
* Supports multiple `.bib` files if needed.
